page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused instance powered by 64-bit Arm architecture (arm64) processors. The configuration features 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It operates without integrated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs. Additionally, local storage is absent, requiring instances to utilize external network-attached block storage for operating system images and persistent data. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with this instance type.

The resource distribution of the n4a-highcpu-32 establishes a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. This resource density aligns with workloads where computational throughput across multiple threads takes priority over heavy per-core memory allocation. Arm64 execution cores offer high multi-threaded compute density, enabling efficient instruction throughput for native 64-bit Arm workloads. However, applications requiring large in-memory footprints or significant local scratch space without network storage overhead may find the 2.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation and absence of local disks restrictive.

This instance configuration is targeted at parallelized compute workloads. Common operational fits include continuous integration and software build pipelines, distributed batch processing, microservice clusters, video transcoding, and web application serving that do not depend on massive memory caches or specialized accelerator hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-32 is an arm64-based compute-oriented virtual machine designed for processor-intensive operations. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio that provides 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned. The server also contains no local storage, necessitating reliance on network-attached storage infrastructure for filesystem persistence and boot media. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. The hardware profile yields an efficient compute footprint for multi-threaded instruction execution on Arm architecture, trading off local disk performance and expansive memory capacity for high core density. Consequently, the n4a-highcpu-32 is suited for horizontally scalable, CPU-heavy tasks such as continuous integration build pipelines, code compilation, video transcoding, distributed batch data processing, and microservice backends that do not demand large in-memory caches.
